questions.stem:
Identify conjugate acid-base pair from following equilibrium reaction.
$\mathrm{HSO^{-}_{3(aq)} + H_3O^{+}_{(aq)} \rightleftharpoons H_2SO_3 + H_2O}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: A conjugate acid-base pair differs by exactly one proton ($\mathrm{H^+}$).
Step 2: $\mathrm{HSO_3^-}$ accepts a proton from $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ to become $\mathrm{H_2SO_3}$, so $\mathrm{H_2SO_3}$ (acid) and $\mathrm{HSO_3^-}$ (base) form a conjugate pair; the other pair is $\mathrm{H_3O^+}/\mathrm{H_2O}$.
Final Answer: (A) $\mathrm{H_2SO_3}$ and $\mathrm{HSO_3^{-}}$
Quick Tip: Check the formulas: the two members of a conjugate pair differ by only one $\mathrm{H^+}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following has highest reactivity towards nucleophilic substitution reaction involving cleavage of $\mathrm{C-Cl}$ bond?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Aryl halides undergo nucleophilic substitution through a carbanion (Meisenheimer) intermediate, which is stabilised by electron-withdrawing $\mathrm{-NO_2}$ groups at ortho and para positions.
Step 2: More o/p $\mathrm{-NO_2}$ groups give more stabilisation: 2,4,6-trinitro (three groups) > 2,4-dinitro > p-nitro > chlorobenzene. 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene reacts even with warm water.
Final Answer: (D) 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene
Quick Tip: Chlorobenzene needs 623 K and NaOH; each extra o/p $\mathrm{-NO_2}$ lowers the required temperature.

questions.stem:
In a reaction,
$\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHMgBr + CO_2 \xrightarrow[ether]{dry} A \xrightarrow[dil\,HCl]{H.OH} B}$.
Find the product ' B ' of above reaction.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Grignard reagents add to $\mathrm{CO_2}$ to give a magnesium carboxylate: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHMgBr + CO_2 \rightarrow (CH_3)_2CHCOOMgBr}$ (A).
Step 2: Acidic hydrolysis gives the acid: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHCOOMgBr + H_2O \xrightarrow{H^+} (CH_3)_2CHCOOH + Mg(OH)Br}$.
Step 3: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHCOOH}$ has a 3-carbon main chain with a methyl on C-2: 2-methylpropanoic acid.
Final Answer: (B) 2-Methyl propanoic acid
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{RMgX + CO_2}$ then $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ gives $\mathrm{RCOOH}$, one carbon more than R.

questions.stem:
If $\mathrm{E^\circ\left(Fe^{+2}_{(aq)} \mid Fe_{(s)}\right) = -0.44\ V}$ and
$\mathrm{E^\circ\left(Sn^{+2}_{(aq)} \mid Sn_{(s)}\right) = -0.14\ V}$
What is standard emf of cell containing the two electrodes?
questions.solution:
Step 1: The electrode with lower reduction potential (Fe, $-0.44$ V) is the anode; Sn ($-0.14$ V) is the cathode.
Step 2: $E^\circ_{cell} = E^\circ_{cathode} - E^\circ_{anode} = -0.14 - (-0.44)$
Step 3: $E^\circ_{cell} = +0.30\ \mathrm{V}$
Final Answer: (A) +0.30 V
Quick Tip: A working (galvanic) cell always has a positive emf; choose the anode so that this is true.

questions.stem: Which of the following molecules contains maximum number of electrons in antibonding molecular orbitals?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Fill MOs. $\mathrm{Li_2}$ (6 e): $\sigma 1s^2\sigma^*1s^2\sigma 2s^2$ - antibonding 2. $\mathrm{N_2}$ (14 e): antibonding $\sigma^*1s^2\sigma^*2s^2$ = 4.
Step 2: $\mathrm{O_2}$ (16 e): $\sigma^*1s^2\sigma^*2s^2\pi^*2p^2$ = 6. $\mathrm{F_2}$ (18 e): $\sigma^*1s^2\sigma^*2s^2\pi^*2p^4$ = 8.
Final Answer: (D) $\mathrm{F_2}$
Quick Tip: From $\mathrm{N_2}$ to $\mathrm{F_2}$ every added electron goes into $\pi^*$, so antibonding electrons increase as N < O < F.

questions.stem: Identify from following reactions that exhibits negative work done.
questions.solution:
Step 1: $W = -P\Delta V = -\Delta n_g RT$. Work is negative (done by the system) when $\Delta n_g > 0$, i.e. the system expands.
Step 2: $\Delta n_g$: (A) $1 - 0 = +1$; (B) $0 - 2 = -2$; (C) $2 - 2 = 0$; (D) $2 - 4 = -2$.
Step 3: Only (A) has $\Delta n_g > 0$, so $W = -RT < 0$.
Final Answer: (A) $\mathrm{2H_2O_{2(\ell)} \rightarrow 2H_2O_{(\ell)} + O_{2(g)}}$
Quick Tip: Count only gaseous moles; gas produced from liquids means expansion and negative work.

questions.stem: Calculate the volume occupied by a particle in fcc unit cell if volume of unit cell is $1.6 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^{3}}$.
questions.solution:
Step 1: In fcc, packing efficiency = 74% and there are 4 particles per unit cell.
Step 2: Volume occupied by all particles $= 0.74 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-23} = 1.184 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}$
Step 3: Volume of one particle $= \frac{1.184 \times 10^{-23}}{4} = 2.96 \times 10^{-24}\ \mathrm{cm^3}$
Final Answer: (B) $2.96 \times 10^{-24}\ \mathrm{cm^{3}}$
Quick Tip: Equivalently $\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}$ with $r = \frac{a}{2\sqrt{2}}$ gives $0.185\,a^{3}$ per particle.

questions.stem: Which amino acid from following contains $\mathrm{-CH_3}$ as side chain?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Amino acids are $\mathrm{H_2N-CH(R)-COOH}$; the side chain R identifies each one.
Step 2: Alanine: R = $\mathrm{-CH_3}$. Leucine: $\mathrm{-CH_2CH(CH_3)_2}$; serine: $\mathrm{-CH_2OH}$; valine: $\mathrm{-CH(CH_3)_2}$.
Final Answer: (B) Alanine
Quick Tip: Glycine R = H, alanine R = $\mathrm{CH_3}$ are the two simplest amino acids.

questions.stem: Which from following medicinal properties is exhibited by curcumin?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Curcumin is the yellow active constituent of turmeric (haldi).
Step 2: Turmeric has traditionally been applied on cuts and wounds because curcumin prevents the growth of microorganisms on living tissue, i.e. it is an antiseptic (as listed in the Maharashtra Board textbook).
Final Answer: (B) Antiseptic
Quick Tip: Natural-product pairs to remember: curcumin (turmeric) - antiseptic, quinine (cinchona) - antimalarial, salicin (willow bark) - analgesic.

questions.stem: Which is the correct increasing order of atomic radii of $\mathrm{Na, K, Mg, Rb}$ ?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Across a period radius decreases (nuclear charge increases), so Mg < Na.
Step 2: Down a group radius increases (new shells added), so Na < K < Rb.
Final Answer: (B) $\mathrm{Mg < Na < K < Rb}$
Quick Tip: Group 1 atoms are the largest in their period; Mg (group 2) is smaller than Na.

questions.stem: Identify the element having highest ionisation enthalpy ( $IE_{1}$ ) from following.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Across the lanthanoid series the effective nuclear charge increases, so $IE_1$ generally rises from La to Lu.
Step 2: Yb ($[\mathrm{Xe}]4f^{14}6s^{2}$) has a completely filled, extra-stable $4f$ subshell and lies near the end of the series; its $IE_1$ (about $603\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$) is higher than Gd (about 593), La (about 538) and Ce (about 534).
Final Answer: (D) Yb
Quick Tip: Filled ($f^{14}$) or half-filled ($f^{7}$) configurations raise ionisation enthalpy.

questions.stem:
Identify the reagent used in the following reaction.
Benzoic acid $\xrightarrow{\text{Reagent}}$ Benzoyl chloride + Phosphorus oxychloride + Hydrogen chloride
questions.solution:
Step 1: Phosphorus pentachloride converts $\mathrm{-COOH}$ to $\mathrm{-COCl}$ with $\mathrm{POCl_3}$ and HCl as by-products.
Step 2: $\mathrm{C_6H_5COOH + PCl_5 \rightarrow C_6H_5COCl + POCl_3 + HCl}$
Final Answer: (C) $\mathrm{PCl_5}$
Quick Tip: By-products identify the reagent: $\mathrm{PCl_3}$ gives $\mathrm{H_3PO_3}$, $\mathrm{SOCl_2}$ gives $\mathrm{SO_2 + HCl}$, $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ gives $\mathrm{POCl_3 + HCl}$.

questions.stem: If $\mathrm{E^{o}\left(Al^{+3}_{(eq)} \mid Al_{(s)}\right) = -1.66\ V}$. What is potential of $\mathrm{Al_{(s)} \longrightarrow Al^{+3}(0 \cdot 1M) + 3e^{-}}$at 298 K ?
questions.solution:
Step 1: For oxidation, $E^\circ_{ox} = +1.66\ \mathrm{V}$ and the Nernst equation is $E_{ox} = E^\circ_{ox} - \frac{0.0592}{n}\log[\mathrm{Al^{3+}}]$ with $n = 3$.
Step 2: $E_{ox} = 1.66 - \frac{0.0592}{3}\log(0.1) = 1.66 - 0.01973 \times (-1)$
Step 3: $E_{ox} = 1.66 + 0.0197 = 1.6797 \approx +1.679\ \mathrm{V}$
Final Answer: (C) +1.679 V
Quick Tip: For an oxidation half-reaction the product ion is in the numerator of Q; lowering $[\mathrm{M^{n+}}]$ makes oxidation easier (higher $E_{ox}$).

questions.stem: A gaseous mixture of $\mathrm{O_2}$ and $\mathrm{CH_4}$ are in the ratio $1 : 4$ by mass. Find the ratio of their molecules.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Take 1 g $\mathrm{O_2}$ and 4 g $\mathrm{CH_4}$. Number of molecules is proportional to moles.
Step 2: $n(\mathrm{O_2}) = \frac{1}{32}$, $n(\mathrm{CH_4}) = \frac{4}{16} = \frac{1}{4}$
Step 3: Ratio $= \frac{1}{32} : \frac{1}{4} = 1 : 8$
Final Answer: (C) $1 : 8$
Quick Tip: Ratio of molecules = (mass ratio) divided by (molar mass ratio) = $\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{16}{32} = \frac{1}{8}$.

questions.stem:
Calculate the relative lowering of vapour pressure of solution containing 3 g urea in 50 g water.
[molar mass of urea $= 60\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ ]
questions.solution:
Step 1: Relative lowering $\frac{\Delta P}{P^\circ} = x_{solute} = \frac{n_2}{n_1 + n_2}$.
Step 2: $n_2 = \frac{3}{60} = 0.05\ \mathrm{mol}$; $n_1 = \frac{50}{18} = 2.778\ \mathrm{mol}$
Step 3: $x_2 = \frac{0.05}{2.778 + 0.05} = \frac{0.05}{2.828} = 0.0177 \approx 0.018$
Final Answer: (C) 0.018
Quick Tip: For dilute solutions $\frac{n_2}{n_1} = \frac{0.05}{2.778} = 0.018$ gives the same answer faster.

questions.stem: Identify the type of defect in brass alloy.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Brass is an alloy of Cu and Zn whose atoms have similar sizes.
Step 2: Zn atoms replace (substitute) some Cu atoms at their regular lattice sites, so brass shows a substitutional impurity defect.
Final Answer: (C) Substitutional impurity defect
Quick Tip: Similar-size atoms give substitutional alloys (brass); small atoms like C in Fe give interstitial alloys (steel).

questions.stem: What is the difference in molar masses of Undecane and Decane?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Undecane $\mathrm{C_{11}H_{24}}$ (M = 156) and decane $\mathrm{C_{10}H_{22}}$ (M = 142) are successive homologues.
Step 2: They differ by one $\mathrm{-CH_2-}$ unit: $156 - 142 = 14\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$
Final Answer: (D) $14\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$
Quick Tip: Adjacent members of any homologous series always differ by $\mathrm{CH_2}$ = 14 u.

questions.stem: Which of the following is effectively used instead of DDT?
questions.solution:
Step 1: DDT is a non-biodegradable insecticide that accumulates in food chains, so its use was restricted.
Step 2: BHC (benzene hexachloride, gammexane/lindane, $\mathrm{C_6H_6Cl_6}$) is an effective insecticide used in its place; $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$, $\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}$ are solvents and picric acid is an explosive.
Final Answer: (A) BHC
Quick Tip: BHC is made by adding $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ to benzene in UV light: $\mathrm{C_6H_6 + 3Cl_2 \rightarrow C_6H_6Cl_6}$.

questions.stem: A compound of Xe and F is found to have atomic ratio $\mathrm{Xe : F}$ as $0.4 : 2.4$, Find the oxidation number of Xe ?
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\mathrm{Xe : F} = 0.4 : 2.4 = 1 : 6$, so the compound is $\mathrm{XeF_6}$.
Step 2: F is always $-1$: $x + 6(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6$
Final Answer: (D) +6
Quick Tip: Xe fluorides $\mathrm{XeF_2, XeF_4, XeF_6}$ have Xe in +2, +4, +6.

questions.stem: A weak monoacidic base dissociates to $1.5\%$ in 0.001 M solution at 298 K . Calculate the dissociation constant of weak base.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Ostwald's dilution law for a weak base: $K_b = \alpha^{2}c$ (since $\alpha \ll 1$).
Step 2: $\alpha = 0.015$, $c = 0.001\ \mathrm{M}$
Step 3: $K_b = (0.015)^{2} \times 0.001 = 2.25 \times 10^{-4} \times 10^{-3} = 2.25 \times 10^{-7}$
Final Answer: (A) $2.25 \times 10^{-7}$
Quick Tip: Convert percent to fraction first: $1.5\% = 0.015$.

questions.stem: Which of the following alkenes does NOT exhibit cis-trans isomerism?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Geometrical isomerism needs two different groups on each doubly bonded carbon.
Step 2: But-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2CH_3}$, has two H atoms on C-1, so no cis/trans forms. But-2-ene, pent-2-ene and 3,4-dimethylhex-3-ene ($\mathrm{(C_2H_5)(CH_3)C=C(CH_3)(C_2H_5)}$) all have different groups on each carbon.
Final Answer: (A) But-1-ene
Quick Tip: A terminal $\mathrm{=CH_2}$ group rules out cis-trans isomerism.

questions.stem:
Identify the substrate ' $A$ ' in the following conversion.
A $\mathrm{\xrightarrow[H_3O^{+}]{AlH_4(-Bu_2)}}$ Pent-3-enal
questions.solution:
Step 1: The reagent is DIBAL-H, $\mathrm{AlH(i\text{-}Bu)_2}$; it reduces a nitrile to an imine which is hydrolysed to an aldehyde, and it does not reduce $\mathrm{C=C}$.
Step 2: Pent-3-enal is $\mathrm{CH_3CH=CHCH_2CHO}$, so A must be $\mathrm{CH_3CH=CHCH_2C\equiv N}$: $\mathrm{CH_3CH=CHCH_2CN \xrightarrow[H_3O^+]{DIBAL-H} CH_3CH=CHCH_2CHO}$
Step 3: Same carbon count and double bond position: pent-3-enenitrile.
Final Answer: (B) Pent-3-enenitrile
Quick Tip: DIBAL-H stops at the aldehyde stage and leaves $\mathrm{C=C}$ untouched; $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$ would give an amine.

questions.stem: The common name of Benzene-1,4-diol is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Common names of dihydroxybenzenes: 1,2 - catechol; 1,3 - resorcinol; 1,4 - quinol (hydroquinone). Pyrogallol is benzene-1,2,3-triol.
Step 2: Benzene-1,4-diol is therefore quinol.
Final Answer: (C) Quinol
Quick Tip: Order o, m, p = Catechol, Resorcinol, Quinol (C-R-Q).

questions.stem: Which of the following is the molecular formula of halous acid of chlorine?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Names of chlorine oxoacids: HOCl hypochlorous (hypohalous), $\mathrm{HClO_2}$ chlorous (halous), $\mathrm{HClO_3}$ chloric (halic), $\mathrm{HClO_4}$ perchloric (perhalic).
Step 2: The halous acid has Cl in +3 state: $\mathrm{HClO_2}$.
Final Answer: (B) $\mathrm{HClO_2}$
Quick Tip: Oxidation states of Cl: hypo-ous +1, -ous +3, -ic +5, per-ic +7.

questions.stem: Calculate the enthalpy of solution of potassium chloride if its $\Delta_{L}H = 700\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ and $\Delta_{hyd}H = -680\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Dissolution = breaking the lattice (lattice enthalpy, endothermic) + hydrating the ions: $\Delta_{sol}H = \Delta_L H + \Delta_{hyd}H$.
Step 2: $\Delta_{sol}H = 700 + (-680) = 20\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
Final Answer: (A) $20\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
Quick Tip: Positive $\Delta_{sol}H$ means KCl dissolves endothermically, which is why the solution cools.

questions.stem:
Calculate the number of atoms present in 1 g of an element if it forms fcc unit cell structure.
$[\rho \times a^{3} = 6.8 \times 10^{-22}\ \mathrm{g}]$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\rho \times a^{3}$ is the mass of one unit cell $= 6.8 \times 10^{-22}\ \mathrm{g}$; an fcc cell contains 4 atoms.
Step 2: Number of unit cells in 1 g $= \frac{1}{6.8 \times 10^{-22}} = 1.4706 \times 10^{21}$
Step 3: Number of atoms $= 4 \times 1.4706 \times 10^{21} = 5.882 \times 10^{21}$
Final Answer: (D) $5.882 \times 10^{21}$
Quick Tip: Atoms in mass m $= \frac{m \times Z}{\rho a^{3}}$; no need to know $N_A$ or the molar mass here.

questions.stem: Which carbon atoms of $\alpha - D$ glucose and $\beta - D$ fructose respectively forms glycosidic linkage in sucrose?
questions.solution:
Step 1: In sucrose the two anomeric carbons are joined: C-1 of $\alpha$-D-glucose and C-2 of $\beta$-D-fructose ($\alpha 1 \rightarrow \beta 2$ linkage).
Step 2: Because both reducing groups are used in the bond, sucrose is a non-reducing sugar.
Final Answer: (A) $\mathrm{C-1}$ and $\mathrm{C-2}$
Quick Tip: Anomeric carbon of an aldose is C-1, of a ketose (fructose) is C-2.

questions.stem: What is the coordination number of central metal ion if it forms octahedral complex?
questions.solution:
Step 1: An octahedron has 6 vertices; each is occupied by one donor atom bonded to the central metal ion.
Step 2: Hence the coordination number is 6 (e.g. $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$, $d^{2}sp^{3}$ or $sp^{3}d^{2}$).
Final Answer: (B) 6
Quick Tip: CN 4 = tetrahedral or square planar; CN 6 = octahedral.

questions.stem:
Nitric oxide reacts with $\mathrm{H_2}$ according to reaction. $\mathrm{2NO_{(g)} + 2H_{2(g)} \rightarrow N_{2(g)} + 2H_2O_{(g)}}$.
Identify the correct relationship for consumption of reactant and formation of product.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Rate $= -\frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{NO}]}{dt} = -\frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt} = \frac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{H_2O}]}{dt}$
Step 2: Hence $\frac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = -\frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt}$ (B). (A) has wrong sign/factor, (C) and (D) should read $\frac{d[\mathrm{H_2O}]}{dt} = 2\frac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt}$.
Final Answer: (B) $\frac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = -\frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt}$
Quick Tip: Divide each rate by its stoichiometric coefficient and put a minus sign for reactants.

questions.stem: The solubility product of NiS is $4.9 \times 10^{-5}$ at 298 K . Calculate its solubility in $\mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$ at the same temperature?
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\mathrm{NiS \rightleftharpoons Ni^{2+} + S^{2-}}$, so $K_{sp} = s \times s = s^{2}$.
Step 2: $s = \sqrt{4.9 \times 10^{-5}} = \sqrt{49 \times 10^{-6}} = 7.0 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$
Final Answer: (B) $7.0 \times 10^{-3}$
Quick Tip: Rewrite the exponent as even ($49 \times 10^{-6}$) before taking the square root.

questions.stem: Which among the following statements is true for haloalkyne?
questions.solution:
Step 1: In a haloalkyne the halogen is on a carbon of the $\mathrm{C\equiv C}$ triple bond, e.g. $\mathrm{HC\equiv C-Cl}$; such carbons are sp hybridised.
Step 2: (B) describes vinylic halides, (C) allylic halides and (D) aryl halides.
Final Answer: (A) Halogen atom is bonded to 'sp' hybridised carbon atom.
Quick Tip: Triple-bond carbon = sp, double-bond carbon = $sp^{2}$, single-bonded carbon = $sp^{3}$.

options.text: Halogen atom is bonded to 'sp' hybridised carbon atom.
Halogen atom is bonded to ' $sp^{2}$, hybridised carbon atom of aliphatic chain.
Halogen atom is bonded to ' $sp^{3}$, hybridised carbon atom next to a carbon-carbon double bond.
Halogen atom is bonded to ' $sp^{2}$ ' hybridised carbon atom of aromatic ring.

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct IUPAC name of catechol?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Catechol is o-dihydroxybenzene: two OH groups on adjacent ring carbons.
Step 2: Its IUPAC name is benzene-1,2-diol (1,3-diol is resorcinol, 1,4-diol is quinol).
Final Answer: (A) Benzene-1,2-diol
Quick Tip: Catechol = ortho = 1,2.

questions.stem: Which of the following halogen forms maximum number of oxoacids?
questions.solution:
Step 1: F, being most electronegative and without d orbitals, forms only HOF. Br forms HOBr, $\mathrm{HBrO_3}$, $\mathrm{HBrO_4}$.
Step 2: Iodine, the largest halogen, can show coordination number 6 with oxygen and so forms HOI, $\mathrm{HIO_3}$ and several periodic acids: $\mathrm{HIO_4}$ (meta), $\mathrm{H_5IO_6}$ (ortho/para), $\mathrm{H_3IO_5}$ (meso) and $\mathrm{H_4I_2O_9}$ - more than Cl ($\mathrm{HOCl, HClO_2, HClO_3, HClO_4}$).
Final Answer: (D) I
Quick Tip: Large size and low electronegativity let iodine form many oxoacids (periodic acids); fluorine forms only one.

questions.stem: Calculate the change in internal energy of the system if 20 kJ work is done on the system and it releases 10 kJ heat in a particular reaction.
questions.solution:
Step 1: First law: $\Delta U = q + W$; work done on the system $W = +20\ \mathrm{kJ}$, heat released $q = -10\ \mathrm{kJ}$.
Step 2: $\Delta U = -10 + 20 = +10\ \mathrm{kJ}$
Final Answer: (C) 10 kJ
Quick Tip: Energy entering the system (heat absorbed, work done on it) is positive; energy leaving is negative.

questions.stem: Which from following solutions exhibits minimum boiling point elevation under identical conditions? (Assume complete dissociation)
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\Delta T_b = iK_b m$; with the same solvent $\Delta T_b \propto i \times m$.
Step 2: KCl: $2 \times 0.2 = 0.4$; NaCl: $2 \times 0.1 = 0.2$; $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$: $4 \times 1 = 4$; $\mathrm{MgCl_2}$: $3 \times 0.05 = 0.15$
Step 3: The smallest effective molality is 0.15 for $\mathrm{MgCl_2}$.
Final Answer: (D) $0.05\ \mathrm{m\,MgCl_2}$
Quick Tip: Always compare $i \times m$ (total particle molality), not m alone.

questions.stem: Identify a monomer used in preparation of neoprene.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Neoprene is polychloroprene, formed by free-radical addition polymerisation of chloroprene.
Step 2: $\mathrm{n\,CH_2=C(Cl)-CH=CH_2 \rightarrow [-CH_2-C(Cl)=CH-CH_2-]_n}$; chloroprene is 2-chloro-1,3-butadiene.
Final Answer: (B) 2-chloro-1,3-butadiene
Quick Tip: Isoprene (2-methyl-1,3-butadiene) gives natural rubber; 1,3-butadiene is used in Buna rubbers.

questions.stem: Identify neutral ligand from following?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Carbonyl is the CO molecule bonded through C; it carries no charge.
Step 2: Sulphato ($\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$), oxalato ($\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}}$) and bromo ($\mathrm{Br^-}$) are anionic ligands.
Final Answer: (A) Carbonyl
Quick Tip: Anionic ligand names end in -o (chlorido, oxalato); neutral ones keep special names (aqua, ammine, carbonyl).

questions.stem: Which from following is used as catalyst in Fisher Tropsch process for the synthesis of gasoline?
questions.solution:
Step 1: The Fischer-Tropsch process converts water gas ($\mathrm{CO + H_2}$) into liquid hydrocarbons (gasoline).
Step 2: $\mathrm{nCO + (2n+1)H_2 \xrightarrow{Co-Th} C_nH_{2n+2} + nH_2O}$; the catalyst is a cobalt-thorium alloy.
Final Answer: (B) $\mathrm{Co-Th}$
Quick Tip: Ni is used for hydrogenation of oils, Fe (with Mo promoter) for the Haber process.

questions.stem:
For a reaction,
$\mathrm{A + B \longrightarrow}$ product, it is found that rate law is $\mathrm{r = k[A]^{1.5}[B]^{2.5}}$. What is the order of reaction?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Overall order = sum of the exponents in the experimental rate law.
Step 2: Order $= 1.5 + 2.5 = 4$
Final Answer: (D) 4
Quick Tip: Order comes from the rate law, not from the balanced equation.

questions.stem: Which of the following ion exihibits maximum power of coagulation for positively charged Sol ?
questions.solution:
Step 1: A positive sol is coagulated by anions; by the Hardy-Schulze rule coagulating power rises steeply with the charge of the oppositely charged ion.
Step 2: Charges: $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ (1) < $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ (2) < $\mathrm{PO_4^{3-}}$ (3) < $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}}$ (4).
Final Answer: (D) $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}}$
Quick Tip: Positive sol (e.g. $\mathrm{Fe(OH)_3}$) - look at anion charge; negative sol - look at cation charge.

questions.stem: Which among the following is NOT Allylic halide?
questions.solution:
Step 1: In an allylic halide X is on the $sp^{3}$ carbon directly next to $\mathrm{C=C}$, i.e. $\mathrm{C=C-C-X}$.
Step 2: In (A), (B), (C) X is on the $\mathrm{CH_2}$ attached to the double bond. In (D), $\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CH_2-CH_2-X}$, X is two carbons away from $\mathrm{C=C}$ (homoallylic), so it is not allylic.
Final Answer: (D) $\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CH_2-CH_2-X}$
Quick Tip: Allylic = one carbon between X and the $\mathrm{C=C}$; vinylic = X on the $\mathrm{C=C}$ carbon itself.

questions.stem:
Identify product ' $B$ ' in the following sequence of reaction.
Aniline $\mathrm{\xrightarrow[273\,K]{NaNO_2+HCl} A \xrightarrow[\Delta]{H_2O} B + N_2\uparrow}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Diazotisation: $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2 + NaNO_2 + 2HCl \xrightarrow{273\,K} C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- (A) + NaCl + 2H_2O}$
Step 2: Warming the diazonium salt with water: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- + H_2O \xrightarrow{\Delta} C_6H_5OH (B) + N_2 + HCl}$
Final Answer: (D) Phenol
Quick Tip: Diazonium salts are stable only near 273 K; on warming in water they give phenols.

questions.stem: Which of the following species acts as strongest oxidising agent?
questions.solution:
Step 1: An oxidising agent gets reduced; the higher its standard reduction potential, the stronger it is.
Step 2: $E^\circ(\mathrm{F_2/F^-}) = +2.87\ \mathrm{V}$ is the highest, while $E^\circ(\mathrm{Li^+/Li}) = -3.05\ \mathrm{V}$ is the lowest. Li is the strongest reducing agent; $\mathrm{Li^+}$ and $\mathrm{F^-}$ are very weak.
Final Answer: (C) $\mathrm{F_2}$
Quick Tip: Top of the electrochemical series ($\mathrm{F_2}$) = best oxidant; bottom (Li) = best reductant.

questions.stem: Identify isoelectronic pair from following.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Isoelectronic species have the same number of electrons.
Step 2: Ne = 10, $\mathrm{O^{2-}} = 8 + 2 = 10$ (same). $\mathrm{Cl^-} = 18$, Ca = 20; Ar = 18, $\mathrm{F^-} = 10$; $\mathrm{K^+} = 18$, $\mathrm{Al^{3+}} = 10$.
Final Answer: (A) Ne and $\mathrm{O^{--}}$
Quick Tip: Electrons = atomic number minus ionic charge.

questions.stem: When 0.01 mole of nonvolatile solute is dissolved in certain solvent calculate the mass of solvent in kg if $\Delta T_{b} = 0.6\ \mathrm{K}$ and $K_{b}$ for solvent= $2\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\Delta T_b = K_b m = K_b \frac{n_2}{W_1}$, so $W_1 = \frac{K_b n_2}{\Delta T_b}$.
Step 2: $W_1 = \frac{2 \times 0.01}{0.6} = \frac{0.02}{0.6}$
Step 3: $W_1 = 0.0333\ \mathrm{kg} \approx 0.033\ \mathrm{kg}$
Final Answer: (C) 0.033 kg
Quick Tip: Molality uses kg of solvent, so the result comes out directly in kg.

questions.stem: Which from following polymers contains $\mathrm{-CO-NH-}$ linkage?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Urea-formaldehyde resin is formed from urea $\mathrm{H_2N-CO-NH_2}$ and HCHO; the polymer chain $\mathrm{[-NH-CO-NH-CH_2-]_n}$ keeps the amide $\mathrm{-CO-NH-}$ link.
Step 2: Glyptal is a polyester ($\mathrm{-COO-}$), thermocol (polystyrene) and Buna-N (butadiene-acrylonitrile) are addition polymers with C-C backbones.
Final Answer: (D) Urea-formaldehyde resin
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{-CO-NH-}$ appears in polyamides (nylons) and in urea-based resins.

questions.stem: Identify the amine having highest $\mathrm{pK_b}$ value.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Highest $\mathrm{pK_b}$ means the weakest base.
Step 2: In aniline the N lone pair is delocalised into the benzene ring by resonance, so it is far less available; aniline ($\mathrm{pK_b} \approx 9.4$) is much weaker than benzylamine ($\approx 4.7$) and the methylamines ($\approx 3.3$ to $4.2$).
Final Answer: (C) $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$
Quick Tip: Aryl amines are weaker bases than alkyl amines; in benzylamine the $\mathrm{CH_2}$ blocks resonance.

questions.stem: The half life values for two different first order reaction A and B are 75 minute and 2.5 hour respectively. What is the $\frac{r_B}{r_A}$ ratio of rate constants?
questions.solution:
Step 1: For first order reactions $k = \frac{0.693}{t_{1/2}}$, so $\frac{k_B}{k_A} = \frac{(t_{1/2})_A}{(t_{1/2})_B}$.
Step 2: $(t_{1/2})_B = 2.5\ \mathrm{h} = 150\ \mathrm{min}$
Step 3: $\frac{k_B}{k_A} = \frac{75}{150} = 0.5$
Final Answer: (B) 0.5
Quick Tip: Convert both half-lives to the same unit before taking the ratio.

questions.stem: Find the number of water molecules in 1 mL of water vapours at STP?
questions.solution:
Step 1: At STP 1 mol of gas occupies $22400\ \mathrm{mL}$ and contains $6.022 \times 10^{23}$ molecules.
Step 2: Molecules in 1 mL $= \frac{6.022 \times 10^{23}}{22400}$
Step 3: $= 2.69 \times 10^{19}$
Final Answer: (D) $2.69 \times 10^{19}$
Quick Tip: $2.69 \times 10^{19}\ \mathrm{mL^{-1}}$ (Loschmidt number) is the same for every ideal gas at STP.

questions.stem: Which from following compounds can be obtained by azo coupling reaction.
questions.solution:
Step 1: In azo coupling a diazonium ion (electrophile) attacks the para position of phenol or aniline, giving an azo compound $\mathrm{Ar-N=N-Ar'}$.
Step 2: $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- + C_6H_5OH \xrightarrow{OH^-} p\text{-}HO-C_6H_4-N=N-C_6H_5 + HCl}$, i.e. p-hydroxyazobenzene (orange dye).
Final Answer: (C) p-Hydroxyazobenzene
Quick Tip: Coupling keeps both N atoms ($\mathrm{-N=N-}$); replacement reactions (Sandmeyer, Balz-Schiemann) lose $\mathrm{N_2}$.
